items.passage: Transcript: Hello, this is Bastien Oyelaran from the language exchange club, and welcome back. Normally the whole club meets Tuesday evenings upstairs in Room 446, and we pair each of you with a partner who speaks the language you are learning. This term we have so many new beginners that we are splitting up. Beginners will meet Monday lunchtimes in the cafeteria. Yes, it is noisy. That is actually why we picked it. When everyone around you is talking, nobody notices your mistakes, and new learners speak up more. Intermediate and advanced members keep Tuesday evenings, but in the downstairs lounge, because Room 446 is booked for exams until midterms. Returning members can keep last term's partner if you tell us by Friday; otherwise you will be rematched. And the Korean and Portuguese tables are full, so if you want either one, add your name to the waiting list at a Monday session. See you there.
items.prompt: [Announcement — Language exchange club] Why does the speaker say, "Yes, it is noisy"?
choices: To present the venue as a benefit for beginners
To apologize to beginners for a crowded venue
To warn members that partners may be hard to hear
To ask members to keep their own voices down
items.correct_answer: To present the venue as a benefit for beginners
items.explanation: The speaker follows the line with "That is actually why we picked it. When everyone around you is talking, nobody notices your mistakes, and new learners speak up more," so the noisy venue is presented as an advantage for beginners. "To apologize to beginners for a crowded venue" is wrong: the speaker chose the cafeteria deliberately and does not apologize. "To warn members that partners may be hard to hear" is wrong: the speaker never suggests hearing will be a problem. "To ask members to keep their own voices down" is wrong: the speaker wants new learners to "speak up more."
